headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/server and broad egress can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with EMQX’s IoT-facing HTTP API.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, so it can ingest external content and tool outputs; EMQX exposes an HTTP API and broad network egress, creating a plausible bridge for attacker-controlled content to flow into MemMachine. No direct provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF EMQX-derived content is forwarded into MemMachine via HTTP API or MCP
IF MemMachine treats received file or message content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any automatic forwarding from EMQX outputs into MemMachine
Require explicit human review before MemMachine executes tool calls from EMQX-fed content
Add a provenance tag to every EMQX message before it reaches MemMachine
Restrict MemMachine MCP access to a test-only namespace
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and can reach out through allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace or relay data, sensitive context can leave the pair; no documented isolation or retention controls are provided, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF EMQX payloads are copied into MemMachine context or memory
IF either agent is configured to relay shared workspace files over its outbound network path
mitigations: Keep EMQX and MemMachine on separate workspaces
Block outbound access from MemMachine except to approved endpoints
Avoid placing IoT payloads into MemMachine memory fields
Review logs for accidental inclusion of user facts or device data
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has HTTP API access and broad egress, while MemMachine offers REST, Python SDK, and MCP Server. The profiles do not show shared writable storage or overlapping mutable resources, so a direct write-write conflict is not evidenced; only a limited coordination risk remains.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable backend or workspace
IF an orchestrator allows concurrent writes without locking
mitigations: Assign separate backends for each agent
Turn on locking in the orchestrator if shared state exists
Schedule writes so only one agent mutates a resource at a time
Audit for overlapping API credentials
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks on shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine’s MCP/REST interfaces make it likely to consume upstream outputs, and EMQX can emit IoT-related data that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. Without a verification step, EMQX errors or malformed payloads can cascade into MemMachine decisions; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses EMQX output as input to planning or memory writes
IF no validation layer checks EMQX payload schema before MemMachine acts
mitigations: Insert a schema validator between EMQX and MemMachine
Require MemMachine to cite source fields before acting
Add a human approval step for any downstream action
Log rejected payloads for review
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on EMQX-fed inputs

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, but the profiles do not show a residency mismatch, regulated data class like PHI, or conflicting certifications. The main issue is a possible retention-policy mismatch if the same data is shared across both systems.
conditions: IF the same personal or device data is stored in both systems
IF MemMachine retains data longer than the EMQX-side policy permits
mitigations: Document retention periods for both systems
Delete shared records on a fixed schedule
Avoid storing regulated data in MemMachine memory
Review access logs for compliance scope
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
